methodological_rigor.justification: Competent methodology for diagnostic comparison study. n=86 lesions (29 melanomas, 57 nevi) from single institution with subspecialist reference standard. Statistical comparisons appropriate (logistic regression, Jonckheere-Terpstra test). Strengths: multimodal imaging for MOLES scoring, blinded assessment. Limitations: single-center recruitment, relatively small sample, MOLES scored only by expert oncologists (not representative of primary care users), MelAInoma applied to historical images not intended for AI.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 3b (diagnostic accuracy study, single center, retrospective). Clinical relevance moderate. Choroidal melanoma detection is clinically important for early intervention and reduced metastatic risk. Both tools are intended for non-expert users but this study only benchmarks against expert MOLES scoring. MOLES widely used in clinical practice; MelAInoma offers reproducible automated assessment but clinical impact in primary care not demonstrated here.

reporting_quality.justification: Well-reported diagnostic study with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, reference standard definition, and statistical methods. Follows STARD principles. Appropriate transparency in reporting model fit and validation (bootstrap resampling, AIC, Hosmer-Lemeshow). However, no code or data availability statement provided. Image quality and patient characteristics well described.

novelty_literature.justification: Incremental contribution. MelAInoma algorithm described previously; MOLES is established scoring system. This study adds comparison between the two approaches but offers no new diagnostic insights or methodological advances. Value is primarily in showing equivalence/complementarity of existing tools rather than advancing the field.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written, clear methods and results. Appropriate discussion of limitations (single-center, expert MOLES scoring not representative of primary care). Figures and tables effectively communicate diagnostic performance. Statistical reporting thorough and transparent.

key_strengths: Appropriate reference standard: subspecialist diagnoses with multimodal imaging and minimum 5-year follow-up for nevi.
Rigorous statistical analysis including bootstrap internal validation with optimism correction (AUC 0.92).
Clear demonstration that MOLES and MelAInoma capture partly distinct information (R²=0.16), supporting complementary use.
Transparent reporting of model fit and calibration; practical discussion of cost-effectiveness considerations.
key_concerns: Single-center, retrospective cohort limits generalizability; all lesions from tertiary ocular oncology referral center.
MOLES scored only by expert oncologists; results not representative of intended primary care users (opticians, general ophthalmologists).
Modest sample size (n=86); wider confidence intervals for subgroup analyses (standard vs. ultra-widefield).
MelAInoma scores applied to historical photographs not originally intended for AI analysis; algorithm development cohort partially overlaps with test cohort.
No long-term treatment outcome data; diagnoses based on clinical assessment without histopathologic confirmation.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid diagnostic comparison study with rigorous statistics but limited scope. LoE 3b, appropriate for Tier 3 journals. Minor revisions needed to clarify generalizability to primary care settings and provide data availability statement.
